instructions: Up to 4 days ahead, heat the oven to 375°F. Brush 1 tsp of the vegetable oil into all 12 cups of a muffin pan.
Put the 2/3 cup raisins in a small bowl and cover them with hot water.
In a large bowl, whisk the 2 cups flour, the brown sugar, 2 tsp baking soda, 1 tbsp cinnamon, 1 tsp ginger and 1/2 tsp salt. Pack the brown sugar when you measure it.
Peel the carrots and shred them on the large holes of a box grater. That should be about 2 cups.
Peel, core and shred the apple.
Juice the orange. That should be about 1/4 cup.
In another bowl, beat the 3 eggs with the rest of the oil, the orange juice and 2 tsp vanilla.
Drain the raisins and squeeze out the water with your hands.
Add the egg mixture to the flour along with the raisins, carrots, apple, walnuts, 1/2 cup coconut and 1/3 cup wheat germ. Stir until there are no dry streaks left.
Divide the batter between the 12 cups. They'll be very full.
Bake for about 25 minutes, until they're domed and a skewer in the middle of one comes out clean. This makes 12 muffins.
Cool them in the pan for 5 minutes, then turn them out onto a rack to cool completely.

They keep in a sealed container on the counter for up to 4 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months. In the morning, eat one as it is, or wrap a frozen one in foil and warm it in a 350°F oven for about 15 minutes.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the muffins up to 4 days ahead.
method_notes: Both fill muffins with grated carrot and apple, raisins and walnuts in a whole wheat batter spiced with cinnamon and ginger. Once Upon a Chef (the lead) soaks the raisins, adds orange juice, coconut and wheat germ, uses oil and three eggs and bakes them at 375°F until they dome. Love and Lemons mixes white and whole wheat flour, swaps some oil for applesauce, leaves out the coconut and bakes them at 400°F, and it gives the 4 day keeping time. This one follows the lead's 12 muffins as written.
